meta.title: Beyond Data formula register
meta.confidence_scale: 100 arithmetic/physics · 90 regulation, tariff or standard read directly · 80 government dataset or statistic · 70 peer-reviewed coefficient transferred from another context · 60 derived with stated assumption · 50 operator or industry claim · 40 proxy · 20 judged · 0 gap
meta.rule: A quantity's confidence is the lowest of its inputs; a condition's is the lowest of its quantities; a match fails at its weakest link; burdens are recorded beside, never netted.

meta.security_note: Security rule corrected 11 Oct 2026: J.B. never set "no security details of real facilities"; that was Claude's caution. The working line is narrower: nothing that works as a guide to defeating security (blind spots, coverage gaps, entry or loading routes, equipment models, staffing times). Surveillance as experienced from public space — visible cameras, signs, indicative watched areas, how it feels — is in scope.
meta.sound_note: Sound is one small component of many (J.B., 11 Oct); it appears on the "as experienced" sheet only and must not dominate the experiential heading.

meta.verdict_states_note: Condition states (met / with a change / not met / not applicable or declined / not yet known / not judged) describe single conditions only. There is no match verdict: decided 13 Oct 2026 — the tool lays out trade-offs by party and does not rank or score options. Wording is suggested for J.B. to accept.
meta.source_roles_note: source_roles (added 12 Oct 2026): for each source, the term of the formula it supplies, its role (coefficient · bound · proxy · check · site fact · rule · data · method · gap) and its own confidence on the register scale; verified=false marks a placement that is Claude's reading of the coefficient text rather than an explicit tie, for J.B. to confirm. A quantity's own confidence is not recomputed from these: it was set in verification and can sit below its sources where the transfer or an assumption is the weak link (status says why), or above a source used only as a check or bound. The md lists every quantity where own confidence differs from the lowest coefficient-role source, for review.
meta.calibration_note: Calibrated 13 Oct 2026 against built cases (sources/13_calibration_cases.md; calibrate.py; calibration_report.md): COP formula changed to full Lorenz with η 0.40–0.50; utilisation band widened to 0.20–0.60; heat_captured (E_reuse) added and ERF redefined to ISO/IEC 30134-6; heat_delivered renamed 'heat available' and the match quantity capped by receiver demand; two ownership models recorded (utility-owned free-heat; supplier-owned paid).

steps: build every combination the tool knows (size, position on the parcel or another parcel, adjacency, technology, both cities, in or out of town)
report the gates first — grid connection (r_grid) and zoning use (z_use): a blocked gate is named before any exchange is weighed, and the exchanges still show as "if the gate moved"
set aside options that break a user limit — and keep them for the "if you moved this limit" panel
drop options worse than another on every row for every party (not a trade-off)
compare positions in the building as options where the user has not fixed one (basement · ground · upper floor · roof), each with its floor load, fuel, flood, vibration and street-front rows
pick as many as the user asked for, as different as possible on the rows the user emphasised

let the user try things on any option — "what if we added…" — whether an opportunity for the place (a seasonal heat store, cooling for neighbours, batteries for the grid), something the place offers (reclaimed water, neighbours' greywater, the ground), or a technology choice (solar, water recovery, cleaner backup power) — and show what each changes and the rules in each city
show them side by side, in no order, each with its full trade-off table
run each option through the four futures (as planned · tenant changes cooling · tenant leaves · receiver leaves) and show what changes

try_menu.name: Rainwater for cooling

rules.vancouver: allowed: rainwater may be used as cooling-tower make-up (VBBL 2025 Table 2.7.1.3); operating permit and professional design
rules.edmonton: alternative solution from the City needed; City must support and oversee monitoring (Alberta notice, 2021)

try_menu.readiness_basis: Microsoft, Netherlands and Ireland, partial (operator claim, no figures).

try_menu.name: Treated city wastewater for cooling

rules.edmonton: precedent at Gold Bar; Water Act authorisation

try_menu.readiness_basis: Loudoun Water reclaimed-water supply to data centres for cooling (utility).

try_menu.name: Greywater recycling

rules.vancouver: not for cooling: greywater only as NSF 350 Class R, reused in the same dwelling unit (VBBL 2025 Art. 2.7.1.2(3))

try_menu.readiness_basis: None found; a data centre has too few occupants to make much greywater.
try_menu.tier_note: engineering only (J.B. triage 30 Oct 2026, item 41; applied 2 Nov 2026)

try_menu.name: Blackwater treatment on site

rules.edmonton: alternative solution needed; Alberta Environment authorisation likely (Alberta notice, 2021)

try_menu.tier_note: engineering only (J.B. triage 30 Oct 2026, item 42; applied 2 Nov 2026)

try_menu.name: Recover blowdown
try_menu.readiness_basis: Quincy Water Reuse Utility, operating since 2021 (US EPA).
try_menu.tier_note: engineering only (J.B. triage 30 Oct 2026, item 43; applied 2 Nov 2026)

try_menu.name: Solar on the roof

rules.vancouver: export ≤100 kW per phase at 10 ¢/kWh (RS 2289), only for sites supplied at distribution voltage — not for a large data centre on transmission service (RS 1830); extra height at the Director of Planning's discretion (s. 10.1.1(d); bulletin, Nov 2022)
rules.edmonton: no development permit for a compliant solar collector (ZB 20001 s. 7.120 cl. 3.7); collectors must stay inside the roof edge; the 1.5 m height allowance is written for residential zones only, so industrial zones are not addressed — City to confirm (s. 5.10 cl. 11); self-supply exempt only when used on the property (EUA s. 2(1)(b), consolidated 2026); anything leaving the site goes through the power pool (s. 18(2)) or micro-generation ≤5 MW

try_menu.readiness_basis: Equinix ME1 Melbourne, 1 MW rooftop (operator claim). None found in Canada.

try_menu.name: Solar on the facade

rules.vancouver: export ≤100 kW per phase at 10 ¢/kWh (RS 2289), only for sites supplied at distribution voltage — not for a large data centre on transmission service (RS 1830); extra height at the Director of Planning's discretion (s. 10.1.1(d); bulletin, Nov 2022)
rules.edmonton: no development permit for a compliant solar collector (ZB 20001 s. 7.120 cl. 3.7); collectors must stay inside the roof edge; the 1.5 m height allowance is written for residential zones only, so industrial zones are not addressed — City to confirm (s. 5.10 cl. 11); self-supply exempt only when used on the property (EUA s. 2(1)(b), consolidated 2026); anything leaving the site goes through the power pool (s. 18(2)) or micro-generation ≤5 MW

try_menu.readiness_basis: MAD01 Madrid, 600 kWp PV facade on 3,600 m² (vendor claim).

try_menu.name: Cleaner backup power
changes: NOx and PM ↓ only with batteries or fuel cells
try_menu.readiness_basis: LCL Aalst, Belgium, gensets on HVO100 (vendor claim); Microsoft Sweden on ≥50% renewable diesel (operator claim). Alberta approvals found are conventional diesel.
try_menu.tier_note: engineering only (J.B. triage 30 Oct 2026, item 36; applied 2 Nov 2026)

try_menu.name: Borefield heat sink
changes: ground warms unless heat is taken out
try_menu.readiness_basis: Epic Systems, Wisconsin: 3.5 MW data centre rejecting heat to 6,100 wells and lakes (US DOE). UBC Okanagan study found steady-state operation not feasible for 250 kW.

try_menu.name: Seasonal heat store

rules.vancouver: boreholes as borefield; aquifer store: water licence
rules.edmonton: boreholes as borefield; aquifer store: Water Act approval or licence

try_menu.readiness_basis: Aquifer store: Equinix Amsterdam with the University of Amsterdam (RVO). Borehole store with data-centre heat: studies only (Stavanger 2023; Li et al. 2021).
try_menu.merged: 2 Nov 2026: aquifer heat store merged in (J.B. triage 30 Oct 2026)

try_menu.name: Deep geothermal
try_menu.readiness_basis: Only electricity contracts found (Google–Fervo, operator claim); no direct heat or cooling link.

try_menu.name: Hot or chilled water tank
try_menu.readiness_basis: EU demonstrations (MODERATOR, 500 kWh store with a 40 kW data centre); Tallaght plans large stores (SEAI).
try_menu.tier_note: engineering only (J.B. triage 30 Oct 2026, item 11; applied 2 Nov 2026)

try_menu.name: Buy new clean power

rules.vancouver: no route found to buy from a new project directly: only BC Hydro signs with new projects ($74–82/MWh in its last two calls); retail access suspended in 2011, current status not confirmed
rules.edmonton: corporate PPAs allowed and common (over 60% of Alberta renewable projects have one); a virtual PPA settles against the pool, where wind earned 46.9% below average in 2025

changes: new wind or solar built for the grid ↑
try_menu.readiness_basis: Corporate PPAs in Alberta are common (Business Renewables Centre, industry); none named for a data centre in Edmonton or Vancouver.
try_menu.tier_note: engineering only (J.B. triage 30 Oct 2026, item 34; applied 2 Nov 2026)

try_menu.name: Cooling from the inlet or river

rules.vancouver: Burrard Inlet: waste discharge authorization for cooling water; BC guideline ±1 °C (marine), proposed objective "no further increase"; Port of Vancouver category C (60–120 business days); DFO fish screens; the Water Sustainability Act defines a stream as a natural watercourse or body of water and names lakes and rivers but not the sea, so whether Burrard Inlet needs a water licence is still not confirmed (the Fraser River does)
rules.edmonton: Water Act licence; Alberta guideline +3 °C over ambient (1999); river valley plan: major facilities only where essential, utility corridors banned except crossings; frazil ice at the intake in winter

changes: a long pipe through the street or the valley ↑
try_menu.readiness_basis: Enwave Deep Lake Water Cooling, Toronto: water at 4 °C from Lake Ontario (City of Toronto reports); not with a data centre in BC or Alberta.

try_menu.name: Condensate to cooling water

rules.vancouver: condensate is clear-water waste, which VBBL 2025 Table 2.7.1.3 lets be used, treated, as cooling-tower make-up (Column B); operating permit and professional design required

try_menu.readiness_basis: US EPA Athens, Georgia laboratory: about 120,000 gal a month in summer (NREL/FEMP case study), a humid climate and not a data centre.
try_menu.tier_note: engineering only (J.B. triage 30 Oct 2026, item 44; applied 2 Nov 2026)

meta.try_menu_note: What would happen if we added X: any option can try these. Each is sorted by which way the exchange runs — an opportunity (the data centre gives the place), something the place gives the data centre, or the data centre's own technology choice. District heat to a network.basis: Vancouver: TELUS data centre heat to the TELUS Garden thermal energy system (BCUC Order C-1-13, 2013) — a development-scale system, not a city network. Elsewhere: Tallaght, Dublin, Amazon data-centre heat, operating since 2023 (Codema); Meta Odense → Fjernvarme Fyn (COP 4.5, 2020); Mäntsälä. Precedent search 15 Oct 2026.

van: heat sold to others is a BCUC-regulated thermal energy system (TELUS Garden: Order C-1-13); NEU credit for heat returned $32.59/MWh (By-law 9552 Sch. C)
edm: Alberta rule for selling heat not yet read; Blatchford: connection compulsory, net-zero buildings exempt (Bylaw C17943 s. 6, s. 8)

District heat to a network.visual: pipe route from the site to the network, homes within reach

Hospital or campus anchor.basis: Université Laval, Québec: supercomputer heat to the campus loop, 1,150,000 kWh/yr. Equinix Amsterdam exchanges heat and cold with the University of Amsterdam through an aquifer store (RVO, Dutch government). Precedent search 15 Oct 2026.

van: as district heat if heat is sold across a property line

unknowns: the anchor's heat demand and supply temperature

New district with the data centre as hea.basis: Westville, Frankfurt: a new quarter of about 1,300 homes planned with at least 60% of its heat from a Telehouse data centre (Mainova, utility, 2021); 2,400 MWh/yr reported in a 2023 best-practice overview (Bytes2Heat). Old Oak, London is proposed (OPDC: 'thousands of homes', about 95 GWh across five phases, 2026–2040; 9,000 is the homes the development will deliver). Tallaght is a new network but serves existing buildings. Precedent search 15 Oct 2026.
unknowns: who pays for the network (capital split)
heat density of a future district
New district with the data centre as hea.visual: massing of a future district around the site

Warming centre, refuge, clean-air room.basis: No case found of a data centre hosting a public warming, cooling or clean-air room or refuge. Nearest: Vancouver's 111 E 5th rezoning requires "an active, high-quality public realm interface" (City report, proposed); the reverse — data-centre heat warming a public pool — is built in Paris (Butte-aux-Cailles, 2017). Precedent search 15 Oct 2026.

van: people sleeping in it makes that part residential occupancy (Group C, BCBC 2024 definition); separations from the data centre not yet read
edm: same Group C definition (NBC 2020 / NBC(AE) 2023); separations not yet read

unknowns: whether it reaches the people most at risk (2021: 98% died indoors, 56% lived alone)
Warming centre, refuge, clean-air room.visual: room inside the building with its own street entry

EV charging hub.basis: No built case of a data centre sharing its capacity or site with public charging. The reverse is announced in the US: GPU pods at EV-charging sites using idle capacity (Xeal, Sep 2026, operator claim). Precedent search 15 Oct 2026. Here (30 Oct 2026 triage, applied 2 Nov 2026): chargers on the data centre's lot with their own new grid connection; the data centre has no spare capacity to set aside.

van: exempt from UCA Part 3 (MO M104; BCUC G-66-19, 2019)
edm: not defined clearly in legislation; status unclear; most parties saw no need for more oversight (AUC Distribution System Inquiry, 2021, pp. 60, 68)

EV charging hub.visual: stalls drawn to scale on the lot, charger count

Meanwhile uses on land held for growth.basis: No documented interim public use of land a data centre holds for expansion. Closest: sheep grazing an on-site solar park (LCL Gembloux, operator claim), not shown to be expansion land or public. Precedent search 15 Oct 2026.

Greenhouse.basis: Göteborg Energi runs a 130 m² proof-of-concept greenhouse on about 24 °C data-centre heat since 2024 (city utility). In Canada: QScale Lévis heat to a 12 ha greenhouse park, under construction (Québec government); a 3 MW proof of concept in Manitoba (operator claim). Alberta: studies only. Precedent search 15 Oct 2026.

van: greenhouse in industrial zones not yet read

Sewage heat as comparator source.basis: Vancouver NEU: 3.2 MW of sewage heat recovery, expanding by 6.6 MW (City of Vancouver). A comparator that competes with data-centre heat, not a data-centre opportunity.
Sewage heat as comparator source.visual: side by side with data-centre heat

Snowmelt on sidewalks and streets.basis: Holland, Michigan melts about 690,000 ft² of sidewalks and streets with 35 °C power-plant waste heat (City claim); no data-centre snowmelt found. Research 19 Oct 2026.

edm: an encroachment agreement for structures in the road right-of-way (Bylaw 12513): application $300–500, then a fee; over 0.3 m or 5 m² the fee is the owner's assessed land value per m² × the area encroached (2026 fee schedule); whether pipes under a sidewalk count as an encroachment is not confirmed; owners must clear adjacent sidewalks

unknowns: who owns pipes under a City sidewalk

Stormwater held for the neighbourhood.basis: Vancouver: 192 developments manage rainwater on site, about 7,400 L/s of peak flow held back (City claim, to Sep 2025); no data centre named; holding a neighbour's or the street's water is not described. Research 19 Oct 2026.

van: required on site (VBBL 2025 2.4.2.5); holding more than required is not addressed
edm: required on lots over 0.16 ha (EPCOR guideline; Bylaw 18100, now repealed by 19627: clause not re-checked ?)

unknowns: what holding back sewer flow is worth to the city
Vancouver: whether a harvesting tank counts toward detention (City guidance 2025); Edmonton: not yet read
Stormwater held for the neighbourhood.visual: a tank under the yard with the required and the extra volume

Emergency water for neighbours.basis: No private tank found serving a Vancouver or Edmonton neighbourhood; the City's 2018 memo names the gap but not private tanks. Research 19 Oct 2026.

van: non-potable firefighting water: no permit if unconnected and marked (DWPR s. 3.1(b)); drinking water makes it a water supplier with permits
edm: non-potable firefighting water: the building code clause is the same as BC (NBC Alberta Edition 3.2.5.7) and the Potable Water Regulation covers only drinking water; drinking water piped to neighbours would make it a private utility waterworks (Alta Reg 277/2003 s. 1(1)(l)) with an engineer-stamped design: a registration if it only passes on city water, an approval if it draws its own river water or ordinary groundwater (Alta Reg 276/2003 Sch. 1–2, Div. 5)

unknowns: tank volume: not yet verified (the fire-code standard has not been read yet)
Vancouver: whether the site is inside the City's seismic saltwater system
Emergency water for neighbours.visual: a tank with a fire-department connection at the street

Seasonal heat store.basis: Aquifer store: Equinix Amsterdam with the University of Amsterdam (RVO, Dutch government; Equinix 2012 claim). Borehole store with data-centre heat: studies only (Stavanger 2023 warns borehole life could fall from 30 to 10 years; Li et al. 2021). Built here with solar heat only: Drake Landing, Okotoks AB — decommissioned in 2024 (failing parts, gas boilers supplying most heat; ATCO). Precedent search 15 Oct 2026.

van: boreholes: registered driller; report. Aquifer store: water licence
edm: boreholes: setbacks (2018 directive). Aquifer store: Water Act approval or licence

unknowns: land for the borefield on or next to the parcel
whether an aquifer lies under the site

Aquaculture (fish).basis: Fish: Green Mountain DC-Telemark → Hima Seafood trout farm, Rjukan, Norway, 800 m apart, operating at test capacity (operator claim); White Data Center eel farm, Hokkaido, since Jan 2024 (operator claim). Operator claims only — no independent source yet. Precedent search 15 Oct 2026.

Rainwater and reclaimed water.basis: Reclaimed wastewater: Loudoun Water pipes reclaimed water to data centres for cooling (utility). Rainwater: Microsoft claims partial use in the Netherlands and Ireland, no figures (operator claim). None found in Canada. Precedent search 15 Oct 2026.

was.name: Backup power for neighbours in a blackout
was.formula: only behind the data centre's own transfer switch, on a private line, with the utility's written approval; never through the utility's lines
was.coef: BC: supplying anyone but itself, its employees or tenants makes it a public utility unless the minister (UCA s. 22) or BCUC (s. 88(3)) exempts it; an affiliate is a separate person (2026 BCCA 93, law-firm summary); BC Hydro: never energize a de-energized line. Edmonton: EPCOR bars extending a customer's wiring beyond its property (T&C s. 4.4, exception in Art. 8.3 not yet verified) and islanding without written approval (s. 7.6, 7.8). Spare generator capacity in a blackout is what the data centre's redundancy leaves, not sized here. Vancouver has 25 disaster support hubs, backup power not stated | 20 Oct 2026 (opps.js): who would need power most, within 1 km: care homes and hospitals (receivers: provincial licence lists, see receivers_nearby); buildings over 21 m from measured heights (Vancouver LiDAR 2022, Edmonton City 3D buildings) and over 39 m, read against BCBC 2024 / NBC(AE) 3.2.6.1 (residential top floor over 18 m: high building), 3.2.6.5 (firefighters' elevator), 3.2.7.9 (over 36 m: 2 h generator for elevators, fire pumps and smoke fans only); heights to the roof, so approximate. Main heating by CMA, SHEU 2019 Table 4.1: Vancouver furnace 39.25%, boiler 22.77% (M), electric baseboard or radiant 28.95%; Edmonton furnace 75.24%, boiler 19.21% (M), electric baseboard U (not published). BC Assessment's care beds, elevators and heating type exist for Vancouver only and are not used, to keep the cities equal

was.name: Own gas plant: heat with the power

was.coef: reciprocating engines 0.8–2.0 MW of heat per MW of power (27–41% electric, 77–80% total, HHV); gas turbines 0.9–1.7 (24–36%, 66–71%) (US EPA 2015, derived from Table 1-3). Rules: Clean Electricity Regulations, units ≥ 25 MW on fossil fuel, 65 t CO2/GWh from 2035 (held in abeyance in Alberta); Alberta TIER $95/t in 2026, sites ≥ 100,000 t a year; BC: waste discharge authorization above 5 MW of combustion; self-supply legal in BC (UCA s. 1(d)) and Alberta (EUA s. 2(1)(b): consumed solely on the producer's own or rented property); Alberta Reg 117/2026 (read in full): data centres of 75 MW or more from the transmission system may be tethered to new generation or storage able to supply at least their maximum demand, located anywhere (no location is set) and of any fuel (the AESO's first intake is gas only, a proposal); tethered requests are processed first (s. 6); bridged service up to 3 years (s. 9); in a supply shortfall large data centres are cut before everyone else (s. 10); the AESO may require zoning approvals and water licences first (s. 7); the regulation expires 31 May 2035

was.coef: BC: net injection up to 2 MW, set by 24 kW per residential and 100 kW per commercial beneficiary (so 2 MW needs at least 84 households); beneficiaries get bill credits, not power; selling power directly to a neighbour fails the UCA s. 1(d) exclusion; credits at 10 ¢/kWh (BCUC G-64-26); each beneficiary takes at most 10–50% of the credits, by group size. Alberta: under the lesser of 5 MW and the service rating, on property owned or leased or adjacent to it, not more than the site's own use; panels on a leased neighbour's roof could serve the data centre (whether a roof lease counts as leased property is not confirmed); revenue-seeking sites are commercial generators

quantities.name: Heat-pump COP (Lorenz)
quantities.formula: COP = η × T_lm,sink ÷ (T_lm,sink − T_lm,source), log-mean temperatures on both sides (sink supply/return; source in/out); η 0.40–0.50 for built systems (calibrated 13 Oct 2026), 0.50–0.60 upper bound
quantities.coef: checks: ~3 at 20→75 °C; 4.5–5.0 Odense; DEA Aug 2026 waste-heat heat pumps, annual average COP to 70 °C forward / 35 °C return: 3.1 at 1 MW (source 13→8 °C), 3.6 at 3 MW (15→8 °C), 4.7 at 10 MW (27→15 °C); air-source 3 MW 2.8; CALIBRATION 13 Oct 2026 (calibrate.py; sources/13): full Lorenz with η 0.50 gives 4.56 for Odense (27→15 / 40→75 °C) against realised 4.5 (2020) and 4.2 all-in (2021–22, η 0.49 / 0.46); Telia Helsinki snapshot 3.9 at 20/32 → ~80 °C implies η 0.39; Université Laval ~7 at ~15 → 40 °C implies η 0.53; ReUseHeat design 3.6 and Bahnhof simulation 3.7 imply 0.37 / 0.43. The simplified form used in the first attempt (sink supply ÷ (sink supply − source out)) under-predicts at large lifts (3.0–3.6 for Odense) and is retired; observed: Meta Odense heat pumps 27 → 70 °C, COP 4.5 in 2020 (14,020 MWh electricity, 230 TJ heat) and about 3.9 combined 2022–24 (Fjernvarme Fyn annual reports); tool range 3.0–4.5
quantities.status: calibrated on six cases: η 0.39–0.53 built/operating

source_roles.relabel: 30 Oct 2026: check → check (term only: drop '/40' (40 °C return not printed) → 'COP 3.6 at 18–25 °C → 70 °C network')

quantities.name: Sound level at receptor
quantities.formula: screen Lp ≈ Lw − 20·log10(r) − 8; full ISO 9613-2 (NoiseModelling) ‖ 3 Nov 2026 (mitigation): Lp = Lw − 20·log10(r) − 8 − (path reduction), summed logarithmically over the plant groups (roof, yard, indoors; NSW 2021 s. 4.1 'summed logarithmically'; FHWA s. 3.1 energy addition). Only sourced reductions are credited: (1) solid screen around outdoor cooling plant: the lower of NSW 2021 s. 4.3 (8 dB if solid, within 20 m of the source, at least 4 m above the source floor, breaking line of sight to the receiver, 2 m beyond the source if not surrounding it) and FHWA s. 3.5.1 (5 dB at line-of-sight break + 1.5 dB per metre above it; cap 20 dB, s. 3.4.2); FHWA figures are for highway line sources and are used here only to lower the NSW credit (our extension ?); (2) cooling plant indoors in a plant room: NSW 2021 s. 4.3, 25 dB (solid walls, roof sheeting at least RW 47, gaps sealed, louvres at least the Table 4-5 insertion loss); (3) low-noise chiller variant (maker claim): Trane RTAF size 280, 1,010 kW, Lw 98 dBA low-noise vs 101 standard, replacing the basis chiller capacity for capacity; (4) night fan-speed reduction for dry coolers: ΔLw = 50·log10(N2/N1) (AMCA 301 as stated in Mathson 2008 p. 4), only for 0.6 ≤ N2/N1 (Annex A.2, informative), so at most 11.1 dB; heat rejection at the lower speed not checked (?). Source changes (3, 4) and path reductions (1, 2) add in dB through the formula; screens and plant rooms are not combined. No credit: per-unit housings ('enclose'), silencers (case values only), cooling towers (SPX gives 50 log as an upper bound, 'no greater than'), hybrid coolers.
quantities.coef: 18 Oct 2026 (sweep M30–M32; audit/plant_sources_2026-10-18.md): unit count = the units the plant lays out (spares included); Lw per unit: air-cooled chillers 102.8–106.1 dBA per 1.49 MW free-cooling chiller (Vertiv Liebert AFC FH3135/FIZ135, Lp at 1 m 80.0/83.0 dB(A) converted to Lw by the ISO 3744 1 m box, our calculation; 'Preliminary data'; low-noise options not rated), dry coolers 98.5–102 dBA at full fan speed (Güntner GFD ≈2.5 MW; Thermokey 738 kW); towers and hybrid coolers use the chiller ratings as a stand-in (labelled). starter set: scroll chiller 450–850 kW Lw 96–100 dBA (Daikin, AHRI 370); Trane Sintesis Prime RTAF HSE 333–1,010 kW Lw 94–101 standard / 91–98 low-noise, plus size 245 (877 kW) printed as 107 / 103, out of line with its neighbours (brochure RTAF-SLB001-GB p.13; sound rows sit under the 'Eurovent performances' heading but are not labelled Eurovent; checked 18 Oct 2026); the tool takes the 1,010 kW unit (size 280), 98 low-noise / 101 standard, as one unit per MW; screw chiller 99–103 (ISO 9614); dry cooler: Kelvion LF-PD203T4H 94 dBA per fan, 6 fans ≈ 101.8 dBA per unit (our sum of the printed per-fan value), 61 dBA @10 m per fan; seller copy, not on kelvion.com; Güntner small unit Lw 67 dBA (permit submittal); standby diesel open 98–99 dBA @7 m (ISO 8528-10); enclosed: Cummins QuietSite L2 73–76, L1 78–87, weather-protective 89–91 dBA @7 m; CRAC 48–62 dBA @2 m (Stulz, 30–150 kW); transformer 62–63 dB (NEMA contour, unverified edition) ‖ 3 Nov 2026 (mitigation): screen height = max(4 m above the source floor, unit height + 2 m) so both methods reach 8 dB for a receiver level with the unit tops (FHWA 5 + 1.5 × 2 = 8); per receiver the credit is min(8, 5 + 1.5·e) where e = screen top − line of sight from the unit top (receiver height = tallest recorded building on the receiving lot; none recorded → no screen credit there ?); the 20 m test uses the farthest any unit lies from the screen toward the receiver. Mass: solid, at least 20 kg/m² (FHWA s. 3.4.2: transmission loss at least 20 dB(A); Ottawa ENCG allows 10 kg/m² on rooftops with justification). A screen taller than the units conflicts with EVAPCO's layout rule that unit tops be level with or above any wall around them at these clearances (maker; more space or the maker's approval ?); a 3.7 m wall 1.8 m from a chiller cut capacity ≥ 4.5% and raised power ≥ 6% (York, maker claim). Low-noise count: ceil(basis units × 1.489 / 1.010); the layout is still drawn with the basis unit (the Trane unit's size is not in the register ?). quantities.name: Local noise limit
quantities.formula: Edmonton Bylaw 14600 at the property line, no averaging period stated: residential 65 day / 50 night, non-residential 75 / 60 (s.19–22); Vancouver by zone pair, continuous: quiet→quiet 55/45, activity→quiet 60/55, other 70/65; AUC Rule 012 Leq 40–56 + tonal +5 for the grid connection and any tethered generation ‖ 2 Nov 2026 (J.B.): hard rule: BLOCK a set-up or size when the level from the cooling plant with the QUIETER unit rating (low end of noise_level) exceeds the night limit at any neighbouring lot; FLAG (note, not a block) when only the STANDARD (louder) rating exceeds it. Night limit governs: the plant runs 24 h. Measured at the point of the receiving lot nearest the centre of the cooling units: Vancouver By-law 6555 s. 1.2 'point of reception' (a point in the lane or street adjacent to but outside the recipient's property, at the shortest distance to the source; where no lane, street or other public property lies between, any point outside the source's property line); Edmonton Bylaw 14600 ss. 20(1), 22(1) 'as measured at the property line of a property zoned for …'. Where no lot outline holds a neighbouring building, its outline is used, labelled (building, not property line: reads low ?). A lot with no zoning record, or an Edmonton mixed-use or Direct Control lot, blocks only above the looser possible limit (Van 55/65 by source zone; Edm 60) and is flagged above the stricter one. ‖ 3 Nov 2026 (mitigation): BLOCK only when no modelled option, alone or combined (source change + screen, or source change + plant room), brings the QUIETER rating under the night limit at every receiver; when one does, the set-up passes with that option named as required. Options are tried source first (low-noise units or night fan speed), then the screen, then both (Ottawa ENCG Intro p. 1: barriers only after other measures; Part 1 s. 3.3). FLAG when the STANDARD rating would need more than the option the quieter rating needs, or no option is enough for it. Neither by-law limits how the level is met: only the received level counts (Van 6555 ss. 2.1–2.3 'when received at a point of reception'; Edm 14600 ss. 19–22 'as measured at the property line'); Edmonton s. 14(3) nuisance applies whatever the dB level (not modelled).

quantities.name: Water licence required
quantities.formula: BC: yes for open-loop heat exchange (WSR Sch. A item 9). Alberta (Guide to Groundwater Authorization 2023 §6.2): open loop with no water loss and return to the same water body = Water Act "activity" → approval; different water body or any loss → licence; closed loop → none. Flow tier for the aquifer test: Q(m³/day) = heat_kW ÷ (1.16 × ΔT) × 24; a 1 MW loop at ΔT 5 K ≈ 4,100 m³/day → top tier
quantities.coef: Alberta EPA fact sheet, Ground Source Heat Exchange Systems (8 Oct 2025; 2024 edition identical on these points): open-loop systems "are regulated through a Water Act authorization" obtained before construction; application must assess the aquifer's capability to circulate the required quantity continuously, effects on groundwater quantity, temperature and quality, and on household, agricultural and existing licence holders; complex systems need an APEGA groundwater specialist report per the Guide to Groundwater Authorization; water in an open loop cannot be used for another purpose or temporarily discharged; open-loop wells drilled by a Class A driller, return through a separate return well; horizontal closed loop above the water table and vertical closed loop above the base of groundwater protection need no Water Act authorization (Class F installer); below the base of groundwater protection the AER regulates under the Geothermal Resource Development Act; applications via DRAS. quantities.coef: wind alone cut a modelled bank's heat rejection to 83.5–89.5% of still-air (Duvenhage & Kröger 1996, peer-reviewed, numerical: cross wind starves up-wind fans; wind along the bank drives plume recirculation; higher fan platforms recirculate more); field cases 13.6% and 24% recirculation (1971, manufacturer engineers — claim); a hot roof warmed inlet air about 0.3 °C (Wray & Akbari 2008, 70); ASHRAE: recirculation "can be a serious problem" for units with intake and exhaust on one housing; roof air "considerably hotter" cuts condenser capacity; zone geometry approximate (Wilson 1979)
quantities.status: geometric flag from the ASHRAE handbook (approximate); no recirculation percentage formula

quantities.name: Urban heat in the area

conditions.heading: 11 What if we added
conditions.name: Water reuse is allowed for this source and use
conditions.test: city × source (rain, reclaimed, greywater, blackwater) × use (cooling make-up) is permitted
conditions.note: Vancouver Building By-law 2025, Book II (as amended to 1 Jan 2026), Art. 2.7.1.2–2.7.1.3: rainwater and clear-water waste may supply cooling-tower make-up and adiabatic cooling (Table 2.7.1.3, Column B); greywater only from NSF/ANSI 350 Class R single-family systems, reused in the same dwelling unit for toilets, urinals and clothes washers — not for cooling; blackwater may not be collected. Alberta: single-property reuse limited to toilets and subsurface irrigation (P-17-01, archived), other uses by variance; Alberta Health 2021 lists cooling towers with treatment targets. Taking someone else's treated wastewater needs Water Act authorisation in Alberta and falls under the Municipal Wastewater Regulation in BC.
conditions.next_action: a supplier quote or a rule check for the addition

conditions.next_action: a supplier quote or a rule check for the addition

conditions.heading: 6 Regulatory
conditions.name: A data centre is an allowed use in this zone
conditions.test: zoning_status is allowed or case by case
conditions.note: Vancouver: conditional only in I-2, I-1C, I-3 (sub-area A) and FC-2; every other district, including all commercial and mixed-use districts, needs a rezoning (RTS 19744 is the test case). Edmonton: the City says large-scale data centres are Major Industrial — IH, or IM where it existed on 1 Jan 2024; elsewhere a rezoning and sometimes a plan amendment, with a Council public hearing. A unit in a mixed-use building is not an allowed use in either city today.
conditions.next_action: ask the authority (City, BCUC or AUC, utility) — cite the rule

new_sources.tourVAN3: J.B., guided tour of Cologix VAN3, 2828 Natal St, Vancouver (about 2 hours, late Oct 2026; her notes typed in chat and three lobby photos). Her words are kept where a reading could change the meaning. HER OWN DESCRIPTION OF THE SITE (where each fact came from is not stated ?): a converted industrial building, about 5 MW, multi-tenant colocation, outside-air free cooling plus magnetic-levitation chillers, Tier III. OBSERVED: no true front or arrival, entrance hard to find; a fence ('K gate fence', her words) with a video-and-voice intercom where she buzzed security; a ramp up to a front door that had to buzz her in; a vestibule with a guard in a closed-off room with 'bullet proof glass' (her words), a slot to slide ID under, massive screens and cameras; a pass, then a buzzed door into a bright lobby (photos: Cologix sign, seating, a round glass security portal, a black door marked 'NOTICE ENTER HERE' with a card reader, a glass meeting room); to the right of the lobby and open to it, a client hot-desk area with private client offices off it, a client kitchen and a client boardroom; a technicians' room down the hall with two desks and equipment; at the far right side a POP room with fibre running from the street, next to a meet-me room, both behind scanners; washrooms with lockers and showers; through the round portal ('the glass circle'), which 'weighed me and measured me' (how she knew: display or guide ?); the guide used the door to its right with 'biometrics AND a scanner'; a first-floor hall on an 18 in raised floor above the slab with a ramp up (measured or told ?); she could not see any servers; 'electrical boxes (400 A)' on the wall, VESDA and a humidifier (from 'he should be the electrical boxes…', read as 'he showed me' ?); out through a back side door at the back-left corner to a second POP and meet-me room; from that hallway a door to a loading bay with two docks and a room where clients' deliveries are stored; a freight elevator off that room. GUIDE'S CLAIMS: giving power back to the grid 'is not a thing and would never make sense' — expensive and insignificant; they cannot get enough power from the grid; even with on-site generation they would always need a substation connection and power guarantees for clients; latency-sensitive clients would never agree to share; uptime too important; maybe possible with one tenant of steady, predictable demand, still insignificant; generator testing 'the only realistic give-back'; multiple UPS systems and multiple feeds (2N) because they cannot risk an outage (Cologix's own page says N+1: cologixVAN3web); the industry is moving to liquid (glycol) to-chip cooling; 'it' is a closed loop (what 'it' refers to ?); they don't use much copper any more, it's mostly fibre; a fence 'drilled 9 feet underground'; a 24/7 guard; 'only three tenants downstairs', each in a private enclosure with 'the company biometrics and cameras' (whose company ?); every 'server box' has a sensor recording temperature and humidity, reported to a third party that monitors constantly; the second POP and meet-me room are for redundancy; clients 'come over night' (reason for the showers); the freight elevator goes to the second storey, a full floor of data hall. Unclear in her notes: 'about the with' in the client-area note (?). One visit: observations, not measurements. ADDED 30 Oct 2026 (her words in chat, from the guide): with AI servers there is more power for machines that take up less floor area than normal, so the power per area is 'entirly dependent on the clients wishes'; data centres 'arent always at capacity' — sometimes empty racks, or areas where clients are building new enclosures. FIRE (her answer in chat, 30 Oct 2026; told by the guide or seen ?): 'vesda fire system with sniffers everhwhere (nitrogen) and targeted sprinklers rathere than whole building'. VESDA is air-sampling smoke detection; what 'nitrogen' refers to (pipe charge, as at VAN4, or a gas system ?) is not stated. LAYOUT (J.B. 30 Oct 2026, 'yes'): the washrooms (lockers, showers) and the technicians' room were before the glass portal, on the lobby side, as her notes' order shows.
